## Where she sits

![The three layers of power](../images/diagrams/cosmology-layers.svg){fig-alt="Three layers of power: the gods, the forces (the Root-Mother among them, with the Amber Queen, the Shadow-Seller, Perkūno Rūstybė and the egregores), and the Kalba craft with its human schools. Offerings and asking flow up, answers and costs flow down. The Three Laws of Balance, Truth and Memory bind mortal craft."}

*Gods harden into Forces; mortals can only ask or bargain. [Editable source](../diagrams/cosmology-layers.excalidraw).*


## Nature

**Native** Force: the wild grief of [Žemyna](../gods/zemyna.qmd) and [Medeina](../gods/medeina.qmd), fused during the 13th-century crusades (cosmology §3.1; canon D8: she is *not* a synonym for Žemyna). She took shape when the Order emptied Sudovia (1277–83) and made the Dykra her body (Book VI ch. 9).

## Wants

The forest kept; plough, axe and iron stopped. She hates the knights' iron and the cities' stone, and chooses not a prince but "what a prince can give her" (Book V ch. 11).

## Takes (its price)

The **Amber Debt**: royal blood for land lost (canon D7). Her servants pay in parts: Eglė's price, "never sell the forest", falls due at Salynas (Book II ch. 19); wolves leave part of the soul in the bog (rite in [the Iron Wolves](../codex/the-iron-wolves.qmd) §4); Galminas's body. "Kas neiškils, tas liks": whoever does not rise from the mud stays (Book III ch. 9).

## Signs & manifestations

Groans in the earth, roots shifting, sap turning red before a massacre, crows leading columns, a whisper that is leaves. She arrives from all sides at once, and the mouth fills with soil that smells of rain (Book III ch. 29).

## Vessels, servants, claims

**Host:** [Galminas](../characters/galminas.qmd), the dead *žynys* she reanimated, who becomes a grove at Grunwald. **Servants:** [Eglė](../characters/egle.qmd) (Pelkių Eglė, taken in the prologue, Book I ch. 16), the Iron Wolves, the [žaltys](../creatures/zaltys.qmd), [barstukai](../creatures/barstukai.qmd), and devotees such as [Elena](../characters/elena.qmd), who carries her tow-knot sign (Book I ch. 12–13). **Claim:** [Vytautas](../characters/vytautas.qmd), contested with [Perkūnas](../gods/perkunas.qmd).

## Weaknesses

She cannot follow onto the steppe: "no forest, no bog" at Vorskla (Book II ch. 23). Consecrated stone and the axe that comes with the priests defeat her; by 1411 she says she has nothing left to stop them (Book III ch. 29). She fades as groves are felled.

## Arc across the books

**Book VI:** the Dykra is born (ch. 9). **I:** Elena, Eglė and the swamp (ch. 12–16). **II:** the debt of the forest at Salynas (ch. 19); absent on the steppe (ch. 23). **III:** Pilkoji, Galminas and Grunwald (ch. 7–29), her last great act. **IV:** she sleeps (ch. 6) and says farewell through Eglė (ch. 27). **V:** she returns and courts Švitrigaila (ch. 11), reclaims the abandoned groves (ch. 28).
